blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Earth rotates from west to east, making local time in eastern longitudes ahead of western longitudes.
A 15° longitude difference corresponds to 1 hour, while a 1° longitude difference equals 4 minutes.
Always add time when moving toward the East and subtract time when moving toward the West.
Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated by adding 5 hours and 30 minutes to GMT (12:00 PM GMT = 5:30 PM IST).
Crossing the International Date Line (IDL) from West to East requires subtracting one calendar day.

blocks.content: The Earth rotates from west to east. Because of this rotation, places to the east see the Sun earlier and their clocks show a later time. Places to the west see the Sun later and their clocks show an earlier time. This single concept is the key to solving all longitude–time numericals.
This means: 15° longitude difference = 1 hour time difference. Further dividing:
Always remember: East → Add time | West → Subtract time.
What is the time difference between two places having a longitude difference of 30°?
Step 1: Understand what is given. Longitude difference = 30°. Step 2: Recall the basic rule: 15° longitude = 1 hour.
Step 3: Divide the longitude difference by 15. 30° ÷ 15° = 2 hours.
Step 4: Since only time difference is asked, direction is not needed. Final Answer: Time difference is 2 hours.
Common Mistake: Students try to convert into minutes unnecessarily.
Find the time difference for 1° longitude.
Step 2: Convert hours into minutes: 24 × 60 = 1440 minutes. Step 3: Divide total minutes by total degrees.
Final Answer: 1° longitude corresponds to 4 minutes.
Exam Tip: This is the MOST IMPORTANT value in SSC numericals.
If the local time at Greenwich is 10:00 AM, what will be the local time at 30° East?
Always remember: East → Add time | West → Subtract time.
Step 1: Identify reference point: Greenwich (0°). Step 2: Identify target longitude: 30° East.
Step 3: Calculate longitude difference = 30°. Step 4: Convert degrees into time.
Step 5: Decide direction. East means ahead in time. Step 6: Add time to Greenwich time.
10:00 AM + 2 hours = 12:00 Noon. Final Answer: Local time = 12:00 PM.
Common Mistake: Students subtract instead of adding.
If the local time at 45° West is 6:00 AM, what is the time at Greenwich?
Step 1: Identify given place: 45° West. Step 2: Greenwich is east of this place. Step 3: Longitude difference = 45°.
Step 5: West is behind, so Greenwich time will be ahead. Step 6: Add time.

rows: Subtract one day (e.g., Monday to Sunday)
Add one day (e.g., Sunday to Monday)

blocks.content: When it is 12:00 noon GMT, what is the time in India (IST)?
Step 1: Remember IST relation. IST = GMT + 5 hours 30 minutes.
Step 2: Add 5 hours 30 minutes to 12:00 noon.
Exam Tip: Never change date unless IDL is mentioned.
A place is located at 97½° East longitude. If the time at Greenwich is 6:00 AM, find the local time.
Step 1: Identify longitude difference = 97.5°. Step 2: Convert degrees to hours.
Step 4: Direction is East, so add time.
6:00 AM + 6 hours 30 minutes = 12:30 PM. Final Answer: Local time = 12:30 PM.

items: The relation 1° longitude = 4 minutes is the most frequently tested value in competitive exam numericals.
When calculating local time from GMT to IST, directly add 5 hours and 30 minutes.
Do not change the calendar date in time calculations unless the problem explicitly mentions crossing the International Date Line (IDL).

blocks.content: A ship crosses the International Date Line from West to East on Monday. What will be the day?
West to East crossing means subtract one day. Step 2: Given day = Monday.
Step 3: Subtract one day. Monday − 1 = Sunday.
Final Answer: Day will be Sunday.
Common Mistake: Students add a day incorrectly.
